sections.label: The opening
sections.line: Hari's stack stays the view; a graph models it
sections.para: Hari Kota asked how I would structure a graph across his ten-layer AI governance stack, so I built it as a vault. His table is kept exactly, every cell a node, and already holds ten cross-layer edges. Each layer keeps its own vocabulary, edges come from provisions, and gaps become queries on a fictional shop.

sections.label: In short
sections.line: The table already holds a graph; gaps are queries
sections.para: Hari's ten layers stay as the view while the graph becomes the model. Ten cross-layer edges exist before anything is added, each layer keeps its own world, and 119 added edges each cite a provision. Missing edges become queries, and dated edges record the 2026 changes under unchanged labels.

sections.label: Hari's stack, exactly as posted
sections.line: Hari's ten layers and forty-six examples, kept verbatim
sections.para: The table runs from Principles and Policy to People and Competence, with forty-six global examples. Hari says gaps appear in layers 3, 5 and 10, and sets a test: name one system's owner and risk tier. The vault checks his eighty-five nodes byte for byte against one transcription.

sections.label: The table already contains a graph
sections.line: Shared instruments in Hari's table already form ten edges
sections.para: Where two rows name the same instrument, role or jurisdiction, they share a node. The EU AI Act links rows 2, 6 and 10 and cites the DPIA; ISO/IEC 42001, NIST AI RMF and Singapore each span two rows; owner assignment links RACI and training. None of those ten edges is added.

sections.label: Each layer is its own world
sections.line: Each layer keeps its own ontology, sharing only grammar
sections.para: Law is articles and obligations, standards are clauses and controls, inventory is systems and owners. No layer adopts another's schema; they share five Fractal Semantic Graphs rules, including meaningful two-way verbs, a ban on relates_to and supersede-never-delete. The vault has ninety-one verbs, each with an inverse.

sections.label: The edges between worlds come from the provisions
sections.line: Every added edge rests on a readable provision
sections.para: EU AI Act Article 26(2) joins law to people, Article 4 covers literacy, Annex III 4(a) covers recruitment, NIST GOVERN 1.6 anchors inventory, and ISO 42001 clause 7.2 covers competence. The graph has 329 edges, 140 between layers, 119 of them added. EU AI Act articles reach nine of ten layers.

sections.label: Zoom from one cell down
sections.line: Zooming from one cell reaches a system's missing record
sections.para: Three of Hari's cells point to the EU AI Act, whose provisions reach Hollow Oak Home's CV screening assistant, its high-risk classification and its HR Lead owner, ending at a missing training record. Every node keeps a breadcrumb back to its cell, and the instrument links out to the Regulation Graph vault.

sections.label: The stack is a snapshot; the graph keeps time
sections.line: Several examples moved in 2026; the graph records it
sections.para: Checked on 9 October 2026: the EU AI Act was amended by Regulation 2026/1744, Colorado SB 26-189 replaced SB24-205, Japan updated its guidelines, and promptfoo joined OpenAI. A table is correct only on its day; the graph keeps labels as posted and records changes as dated edges.

sections.label: Do this today, as a traversal
sections.line: Hari's do-this-today test is a traversal query
sections.para: On fictional Hollow Oak Home's eight systems, five pass the owner-and-tier test, one lacks a tier, one lacks an owner, and one has neither. The CV screening assistant passes, yet walking all ten layers shows three red rows: no HR Lead training record and bias results that reach no report.

sections.label: Hari's three gaps, as queries
sections.line: Hari's three gaps become queries with concrete results
sections.para: Layer 3 finds Singapore guidance tracked by no role; layer 5 finds the transcription tool found in September expenses but missing from the register; layer 10 finds the HR Lead untrained despite Articles 4 and 26(2). Four further queries follow the same pattern.

sections.label: What "4 or 5" means in a graph
sections.line: "4 or 5 layers" splits into three different questions
sections.para: For the fictional shop, ten of ten layers have some complete path, one is complete for every registered system, and none once the expenses tool is counted. Per system the answers are 10, 7, 10, 4, 6, 9, 0 and 9. The graph computes which meaning applies.

sections.label: Bring your own
sections.line: Paste two CSVs and the gap queries run locally
sections.para: Readers can paste a systems CSV and a people CSV, and the do-this-today test plus the three gap queries run in the browser. Nothing is sent anywhere and the vault is never written. The templates hold Hollow Oak Home's data as the example.

sections.label: How the vault is built, and what it does not claim
sections.line: A twenty-two-check gate rebuilds every file; claims are bounded
sections.para: One script writes 335 nodes and 702 edges, exported as CSV, JSON-LD and Turtle, using a research pack of 114 entries marked verified or not. A release gate of twenty-two checks reproduces and recomputes everything. Hollow Oak Home is fictional and nothing is legal advice.

sections.label: Prior art
sections.line: AI law graphs exist; the fractal shape is new
sections.para: Hernandez, Golpayegani and Lewis proposed a knowledge graph mapping the EU AI Act to standards in 2024; AIRO and the W3C DPV AI extension offer vocabularies, and NIST crosswalks are published edges. The vault adds the fractal shape, provisions as edge sources and gaps as queries.

sections.label: Open it
sections.line: Links: the vault, its read key and related graphs
sections.para: The AI Governance Graph vault opens with a published read key and an sgit clone command. Related links cover Fractal Semantic Graphs, the Regulation Graph of the EU AI Act and AI BCF as a graph. Hari's stack stays as drawn, and the offer to extend it stands; not legal advice.
